mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or each UBO's home jurisdiction (e.g. Corporations Canada, Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if home jurisdiction is party to Apostille Convention; otherwise Canadian consular legalization at the Canadian Embassy/High Commission in the home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each proposed director, officer, and individual UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or official issuing authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, officers, authorized signatories, and 25% or more UBOs against (i) the Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (ii) the Criminal Code listed terrorist entities; (iii) the OFAC SDN List in connection with anticipated USD clearing and SWIFT wires; and (iv) domestic and foreign designations made under the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. The screening must include PEP status per PCMLTFA regulations, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for all non-resident UBOs, and an escalating risk profile. For this medium-risk IP-licensing HoldCo, enhanced measures are required when the parent, licensor, or UBO resides outside Canada.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (OBR) at ontariobusinessregistry.ca; NUANS Name Search Report required before filing Articles of Incorporation under the Ontario Business Corporations Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in English or French and may be in a combined English-French bilingual format. It must include a legal element designated under OBCA s. 10, e.g. 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', or the applicable French equivalents 'Compagnie', 'Incorporée', 'Limitée'. Names are recorded in Roman script; no other script is accepted for the legal name. The name must be distinguishable from all existing corporate, LLP, and registered trademark names in the NUANS index, as required by OBCA s. 9.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Trust, Tontine (require federal OSFI approval)
Insurance, Assurance, Loan (require FSRA regulatory approval)
College, Institute, University (require Ministry of Colleges and Universities consent)
Engineer, Engineering (require Professional Engineers Ontario consent)
Physician, Clinic, Hospital (require regulated health profession body consent)
Canada, Ontario, Crown, Royal, Government (require ministerial approval before use)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection by the Director appointed under OBCA, the applicant obtains the written refusal and reason. Where the basis is confusing similarity, the applicant may (i) obtain a written no-objection or consent letter from the existing names user or trademark owner; (ii) amend the proposed name and request a new NUANS Name Search Report; or (iii) request reconsideration through the Ontario Business Registry help-desk by providing distinctiveness evidence. If the refusal is arbitrary or made contrary to OBCA s. 9, the applicant may file an originating application for judicial review with the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, seeking an order directing the Director to accept the name. All administrative and judicial remedies should be pursued before the expiry of the 90-day NUANS report validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a passive IP-licensing HoldCo through a licensed Ontario corporate registered office service provider, provided there is a physical street address in Ontario at which process may be served and statutory records are kept. The registered office need not be the principal place of business. No full-time employee or physical office presence is required for OBCA compliance, though economic substance may be relevant for CRA and treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 2% to 4% unannounced physical on-site inspection risk for a passive medium-risk IP-holding corporation. FINTRAC and the CRA typically conduct correspondence audits and targeted record requests, but a physical compliance visit may occur if the registered office address is used solely as a mail drop without an accessible corporate records location.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, ss. 4, 95, 104, 110, 114 and 115
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: ServiceOntario – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Ontario Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the OBCA; incorporation may proceed with nominal capital. No escrow or trustee capital account is mandated for a business corporation in Ontario; however, the IP HoldCo should maintain adequate share capital or shareholders’ loan balance to cover initial expenses and future IP acquisition costs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The undersigned incorporator subscribes for one hundred (100) Common Shares of the corporation for nominal consideration, and the board accepts the subscription and authorizes issuance of share certificates. 2. The registered office shall be established at 120 Adelaide Street West, Suite 2500, Toronto, Ontario, M5H 4A5. 3. The incorporator is directed to file Articles of Incorporation and take all necessary procedural steps to complete statutory incorporation. 4. Jane Doe is appointed sole director and John Smith is appointed President and Secretary-Treasurer. 5. The director is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, approve a form of restricted stock unit plan, adopt preliminary by-laws, and execute all lease, licensing and IP assignment documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for the proposed corporate name in Ontario. If a numbered company is preferred, confirm no separate name reservation is required. Review search results for conflicting trademarks or existing corporate names; file the name reservation if corporate name will include a distinctive element.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report identifies a conflict, select a new name or obtain a consent letter from the conflicting corporation; resubmit the search request within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) and submit electronically via the Ontario Business Information System. Include the authorized share capital structure, the registered office address, the number of directors, and the full legal name and address of each incorporator. After filing, the electronic system will issue a Notice of Filing and a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (if using a name)
Registered office address (physical address in Ontario, no post office box)
Full names and addresses of incorporators and proposed first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ServiceOntario returns a deficiency statement, correct the specified fields and resubmit within 30 days; if the name is rejected, provide an alternate name or adopt a numbered company designation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Canada Revenue Agency for Business Number and Corporation Tax Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, register the corporation with the CRA using Business Registration Online. Apply for the federal Business Number (BN), GST/HST account, corporation income tax account, and request a separate payroll account only if employees will be hired. Ensure all notifications are linked to the Ontario corporate registry.
required_dossiers: NUANS report and approved corporate name
Names and birth dates of directors/officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA questions the application (e.g., inconsistent director information), provide the missing T2/CORP corporate identification documentation by email submission; if the BN is not issued within 10 business days, contact CRA business line and request expedited processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting and Adopting First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors meeting to adopt the pro-forma board resolution, approve corporate by-laws, fix the financial year end, elect officers, establish the share register, issue share certificates, and authorize the opening of bank accounts. Prepare and maintain minutes in the corporate records book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initial director or officer is unavailable, execute written consent resolution in accordance with OBCA; if share issuance is challenged, re-execute share certificates and update the central securities register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishing Registered Office and Corporate Records Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and Registered Office (physical premises in Ontario)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the corporation maintains a physical registered office in Ontario with proper signage, rental lease or ownership documentation, and a corporate records book containing articles, by-laws, minutes, share register, and financial records. Verify that the registered office address matches the address filed with ServiceOntario.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership documentation for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a compliance audit identifies a missing record, cure by reconstituting the document and filing a corrected Notice of Change of Registered Office if the address has shifted; update the records book immediately.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial or manufacturing operation triggered; general municipal business licensing and landlord consents apply
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: N/A – Statutory industrial operating license not required for IP holding and patent royalty sub-licensing activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative office and IP management operations; no regulated activity, no emissions, no discharge, no venue requiring a full EIA report
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated wastewater, VOC, or particulate discharge threshold applies. If future office build-out or HVAC works produce construction-related waste, applicable O. Reg. 347 waste standards and Ontario Fire Code requirements must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: compliance with Ontario Fire Code and local municipality by-law requiring adequate extinguishers, evacuation signage, and fire department inspection if office occupancy exceeds 300 persons or high-rise conditions. Building safety: architectural/engineering structural load review is not separately required for ordinary office tenancy; occupancy permit must be obtained from the applicable municipality (Toronto Building Division if leased premises in Toronto). Occupational workplace clearance: compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act and Workplace Safety and Insurance Board registration for workers compensation coverage if employees are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – official portal: Canada.ca (My Business Account / GST/HST Accounts)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada or earning Canadian-source income must: (1) obtain a federal Business Number (BN) by registering with the CRA via the 'Register for a Business Number' online service or Form RC1; (2) separately register for a GST/HST account (Form RC1 or online) if the entity makes taxable supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier, or if it enters the Canadian market through a permanent establishment; (3) register under the Ontario Corporations Tax Act by filing Form ON through the Ontario Ministry of Finance if it has taxable presence in Ontario; (4) for IP-holding structures, obtain a non-resident corporation account and complete Form RC820 (Return of Non-Resident Corporation carrying on business in Canada) or file under the applicable income tax return where required. The CRA will issue a BN with a program account suffix (e.g., RTxxxxxxx for GST/HST, RC for corporation income tax), and all registrations must be completed before the first taxable supply or payroll remittance in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime for federal tax purposes. A Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer subject to corporate income tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada). Entity classification is determined by legal form; a corporation cannot elect to be fiscally transparent for Canadian tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch rules under Section 18.4 and the hybrid mismatch arrangements legislation (addressing deductible/franked payments) apply to cross-border IP royalty arrangements. A non-resident entity may, however, choose to be treated as a corporation or a branch/permanent establishment for treaty and Part XIII purposes depending on the existence of a Canadian permanent establishment; this is a factual determination, not an elective mechanism. A GST/HST 'election' is available for closely related corporations to treat taxable supplies as made for nil consideration (Form GST25), and a non-resident can elect to use the 'simplified GST/HST registration' regime. An Ontario 'notional election' may be made to allocate taxable income under the Corporations Tax Act where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a single quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; however, a zero threshold applies to non-resident businesses that 'carry on business in Canada' or that solicit orders in Canada and supply goods or services in Canada. For a non-resident IP licensor with a Canadian permanent establishment or Canadian-resident licensee, the CRA generally requires GST/HST registration regardless of the small supplier threshold unless the supplies are zero-rated exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no federal electronic-invoicing clearance mandate or real-time fiscal stamping framework. The CRA requires business records and invoices to be kept in a readable format, but does not require API-based real-time transmission of invoice data to the CRA. The Business Number must be displayed on all GST/HST invoices where the supplier is registered, and invoices must contain prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act. Ontario does not operate a separate provincial e-invoicing clearance system; the HST portion is administered by the CRA. For customs export purposes, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) requires electronic export reporting via the Canadian Export Reporting System for most exports, with the final export declaration transmitted digitally.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (a) supplies of goods exported from Canada by the supplier or for the purchaser and subsequently exported as part of the supplier's commercial activity; (b) supplies of services to a non-resident person if the service is supplied to a non-resident who is not registered under GST/HST and who is not carrying on business in Canada at the time the service is performed, and the service is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada; and (c) royalties and licensing arrangements for intellectual property where the royalty is paid by a non-resident for use outside Canada. For an ISIC 6420 IP HoldCo sub-licensing patents globally, zero-rating generally applies if the licensee is a non-resident and the IP is exploited only outside Canada. The supply of a patent license to a Canadian resident for use partly or wholly in Canada is subject to GST/HST at the applicable rate (13% in Ontario) unless specifically zero-rated. The zero-rating must be demonstrated by documentation establishing the non-resident status of the recipient and the offshore use of the IP.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Export Declaration (via CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System, Form B13A or electronic equivalent)
Commercial invoice evidencing royalty/license fee and payment terms
Executed license agreement or sub-license agreement identifying the non-resident licensee and territorial rights
Evidence of non-resident status: certificate of incorporation, tax residence certificate, or non-resident declaration
Bank remittance/Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 confirming receipt of royalty proceeds
CRA record-keeping evidence of zero-rated supply claim (e.g., Form GST111 Return or schedule)
Certificate of Analysis/Use if custom authorities require proof of export beyond Canadian territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Excise Tax Act, a false or unreasonable claim for zero-rating may result in reassessment of GST/HST, interest, and penalties. Knowingly making a false statement or omitting material facts can trigger penalties of C$250 or, for gross negligence, 50% of the understated tax. Attempting to evade GST/HST may lead to criminal prosecution with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. For income tax, a royalty payment that is zero-rated but not actually repatriated within 180 days may be challenged under the transfer-pricing rules and foreign-accrual property income rules; the CRA may disallow deductions, impose a 10% penalty on failed cross-border pricing documentation, and reassess Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on the gross royalty. Retrospective clawbacks can cover a six-year period, or indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with exchange-control administration carried out by the Department of Finance Canada and AML/CFT supervision by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; OSFI supervises all authorized banks (Schedule I, II, and III) under the Bank Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange arrangement. Canada does not operate exchange controls; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951. Both capital and current account transactions are unrestricted, and profit or royalty remittances to non-residents are freely transferable, subject only to source-based non-resident withholding tax under Section 212 of the Income Tax Act (Canada), which may be reduced under an applicable income tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline, no surrender requirement, and no mandatory conversion ratio applicable to export receipts or royalty proceeds. Exporters and IP licensors may retain and hold CAD or any foreign currency without central bank approval. Routine cross-border transfer reporting is limited to FINTRAC large-transaction thresholds and Statistics Canada international-transactions data collection for statistical purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with treasury management and Payments Canada clearing access
Operational Account (FX hedging and liquidity lines)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury banking relationship; Medium as a supplementary digital collection rail. EMIs are not recognized as 'banks' under the Bank Act; non-bank cross-border payment service providers must be registered as money service businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC. Digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut can facilitate royalty receipts and disbursements, but they cannot hold regulated deposits, provide CAD liquidity management, issue commercial letters of credit, or offer deposit insurance through CDIC. A regulated Schedule I bank should remain the liability-holding clearing counterparty and treasury anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under OSFI Guideline E-13 using a risk-based customer due diligence model, including video verification and notarized or apostilled identity documents. In practice, Schedule I banks require a live compliance interview with at least one director or the authorized signing officer for non-resident-owned IP HoldCos. Physical appearance by a director at a Canadian branch, or appointment of a local attorney-in-fact with signed authority, is generally mandatory before the full treasury product suite is activated, including FX forwards, borrowing facilities, and merchant services. Pure deposit and wire collection accounts may be opened remotely under enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered global IP ownership with an opaque non-resident intermediate parent chain lacking demonstrated economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance dossier comprising: (i) group organizational chart; (ii) Ontario office lease and staffing evidence; (iii) board resolutions approving decision-making in Canada; (iv) executed intercompany patent and sub-licensing agreements; (v) OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation with royalty-rate benchmarking; (vi) 24-month financial projections and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial owner, nominee shareholder arrangements, or bearer share structures in the upstream foreign parent chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO transparency bundle: certificate of good standing; certified Register of Directors; certified Register of Shareholders; signed beneficial ownership declaration for every natural person with 25% or more control; confirmed corporate registry search from the parent jurisdiction; and a legal opinion from upstream counsel confirming the absence of nominee or bearer share arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty flows to or from jurisdictions on the FATF grey list, OFAC sanctions lists, or Canada's Special Economic Measures Act sanctions list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Programmatic compliance file: (i) SWIFT purpose and payment narrative; (ii) underlying licence agreements and patent registration certificates; (iii) royalty calculation schedules tied to contract milestones; (iv) a Canadian legal sanctions and AML opinion; (v) an annex listing all non-resident payees and their jurisdictions of tax residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital injections and royalty wires that materially deviate from the registered business profile or trigger structuring and territorial-nexus concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical-performance and forecast file: (i) 12-month cash-flow forecast by funding leg; (ii) executed board minutes approving the flow of funds; (iii) sample invoices and remittance advices; (iv) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each capital injection; (v) bank reference letter from the parent's existing foreign bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: upstream parent sends a SWIFT MT103 to the Ontario entity's Schedule I bank, clearing through LVTS for CAD or CHIPS/Fedwire for USD. The wire must include (i) a purpose-of-payment code for direct investment, (ii) a transaction narrative referencing the share subscription or contribution agreement, (iii) matching legal entity identifiers and bank identifiers, and (iv) pre-onboarded beneficiary documentation. The receiving bank verifies source of funds and applies FINTRAC large-transaction thresholds for transfers at or above CAD 10,000. Capital injections are credited to the Capital Escrow Account and are released only upon a director resolution and production of OSFI-compliant corporate records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty disbursements use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 CORR as the default clearing rail; the CAD leg clears through LVTS and the USD leg through the Canadian bank's U.S. clearing correspondents. Where the cross-border agreement bundles physical goods or equipment with the IP licence, a Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit under UCP600 may be used, with presentation of patent certificates, royalty invoices, and transport documents. For pure ISIC 6420 licensing, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 executed under the intercompany licence, with Section 212 withholding evidenced by an NR4 remittance certificate or a treaty-based reduced withholding tax certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forwards under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible in principle where the underlying foreign currency is not freely deliverable in the settlement jurisdiction; generally not required for CAD, which is fully deliverable through LVTS
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD/EUR) for multi-year hedging of royalty receivables and payables
Vanilla FX call and put options purchased from a licensed Canadian authorized deposit-taking institution
FX spot contracts transacted at the Bank of Canada observed rate with T+0 or T+1 settlement through LVTS or correspondent funds clearing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Business Corporations Act Annual Return (Form 1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director under the Ontario Business Corporations Act, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario), Government of Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation, in each calendar year (OBCA s. 113).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late monetary fee; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director to initiate administrative cancellation and dissolution after a 60-day notice under OBCA s. 241. Outstanding annual returns may also prevent issuance of a certificate of status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Ontario corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Ontario Ministry of Finance (administration delegated to CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax payments are due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small-business deduction).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance due under Income Tax Act s. 162(1), plus 1% per complete month late up to 12 months; a repeat late-filer with a demand may be subject to a 10% penalty plus 2% per month. Interest accrues daily on unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T106 Information Return on Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents (cross-border patent licensing royalties)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), International and Large Business Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; filing is required for each taxation year in which aggregate reportable non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500) under Income Tax Act s. 162(10); gross negligence or false statements may attract penalties under s. 163, and prosecution under s. 235 can result in a fine of CAD 1,000 to CAD 25,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The OBCA and CBCA do not impose a revenue or asset threshold for a private non-distributing corporation. An audit is mandatory for offering/distributing corporations, for corporations whose shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued shares have made a formal audit demand, and for any non-exempt corporation that has not adopted a unanimous shareholder resolution dispensing with the appointment of an auditor. An audit may otherwise be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution for each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable or distributing corporations must apply IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I). Private enterprises may use ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II, the applicable Canadian GAAP) or elect IFRS. An Ontario IP holding corporation with solely intercompany royalty income may elect ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For CBCA corporations, the annual return requires a senior officer or director to confirm the location of the Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and that it has been properly maintained. For OBCA corporations, no separate public UBO filing is currently required in Ontario; however, upon any transfer of shares, the register of members must be immediately updated and any individual with significant control must be identified in the internal ISC/UBO records. The board must ensure the register of members and UBO records are available for inspection and are confirmed as accurate at the annual return date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 400 per year for a registered office address and registered agent under Ontario corporate compliance service providers.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 per year for a certified independent audit of a single-asset IP holding corporation with cross-border royalty licensing transactions.
